PSP·01

Science, theory, paradigm

Before we talk about Pokémon, we need to agree on what we’re even talking about: what can be claimed, and on what grounds

Chapter 1/8 · 4%

WHAT IS SCIENCE

Science: a claim that can be falsified

What makes a claim scientific is that you can imagine an observation that would prove it wrong. Science is an endless loop: a claim survives only until the next experiment.

1

Observation

Something in the world keeps repeating

2

Hypothesis

An explanation that predicts what will happen

3

Experiment

Actively looking for what would disprove it

4

Survives or falls

And back to the start

Chapter 1/8 · 5%

SIDE NOTE

Karl Popper, 1934: the falsifiability test. A claim that can't be disproven isn't a scientific claim.

WHAT IS A THEORY

Theory: a system that lets you say something meaningful about the world

A theory is a set of concepts and the links between them. It takes a messy pile of observations and gives it order, names and logic.

Theory in the natural sciences

Gravity predicts exactly where the ball will land. You can measure, repeat the experiment, and falsify.

Social theory

You can’t put a society in a lab. Theory helps us interpret, spot patterns and ask better questions.

Chapter 1/8 · 6%

PARADIGM

Paradigm: the glasses we look through

A paradigm is a framework that decides what we see at all and which questions we ask. Example: Pikachu refuses to get into its Poké Ball.

Education glasses

"He needs training"

Medical glasses

"Maybe he's hurt"

Sociology glasses

"He wants a friend, not an owner"

Same Pikachu, three pictures. What changes is the glasses.

Chapter 1/8 · 7%

SIDE NOTE

Thomas Kuhn, 1962: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions. Science moves in leaps, as one paradigm replaces the one before it.
<section id="s-memory"></section>

PSP = POKÉMON SOCIOLOGICAL PARADIGM

From here: PSP. Three words, three decisions

So far: what a paradigm is. From here: one paradigm. And why Pokémon? Because when a fictional world is rich and consistent enough, its parallel to reality starts to make sense.

P

Pokémon

The language

The world we take the concepts from. 30 years of balancing, for competitive play and for world-building, created a system that balances itself with formulas.

S

Sociological

The subject

People, and the relations between them: how one person affects another and changes within settings.

P

Paradigm

Its status

A framework with internal logic, which lets us say something about something without claiming absolute truth.

Chapter 1/8 · 9%

PSP·02

How the picture is built

151 questions, the people who know you best, and an engine that compares against 600 lines

Chapter 2/8 · 10%

THE QUESTIONNAIRE · 151

151 questions, like the 151 Pokémon of the first generation

I drew on established, research-based personality questionnaires: short statements, a 1–5 scale, several items per trait, and reverse-keyed items that check people are paying attention.

54

Type questions

Statements about the 18 types, on a 1–5 scale

40

Scenario responses

10 life situations, 4 possible responses each

36

Stat questions

6 questions for each of the 6 stats

20

Evolution questions

4 questions for each of the 5 ways to evolve

1

Mew’s bonus question

4 statements built from the result that slightly strengthen the match. The answer here is public

Every question can be answered with “I don’t know”, and it simply isn’t counted. Better a gap in the data than a guess.

Chapter 2/8 · 10%

360° · RATERS

Nobody is the only witness to themselves

Everyone has blind spots, so the people who know the subject best answer the questionnaire too.

The subject is always 45%. The subject splits the remaining 55% themselves, according to who knows them best.

In HP and Sp. Def, which happen mostly inside, the subject's weight goes up. In Attack and Sp. Atk, which others see better, it goes down.

PSP·03

The founders of sociology

Every way of sorting people gets something right and misses something. The question is how much.

Chapter 3/8 · 18%

THE URGE TO SORT

The urge to sort

?

Hands up: who knows their star sign? And which Hogwarts house they’re in?

The urge to sort people into types is itself a social phenomenon. The founders of sociology did it too, each in their own way:

Chapter 3/8 · 19%

Open with the question to the audience and wait for hands. Then: Durkheim noticed this too. Sorting isn’t just a sociologist’s tool, it’s something every society does.

THREE FATHERS OF SOCIOLOGY

Right, and missing something

Durkheim

1

Society as one body: what holds people together is what they share.

Got right

There’s an “us”, and shared values hold a society together.

Missed

Inside the “us”, everyone looks the same.

Marx

2

An arena of struggle between two classes: those who own the means of production and those who work for them.

Got right

There are classes, and there is struggle.

Missed

Two workers can differ from each other more than a worker differs from a factory owner.

Weber

4

Four types of social action: instrumental, value-based, affective and traditional.

Got right

People act for different reasons, and those reasons can be sorted.

Missed

Every real action is a mix of several types.

Chapter 3/8 · 20%

For each one: first what he got right, and only then what was left out. The point is that none of them was wrong. They just saw in low resolution.
<section id="c-memory"></section>

LOW RESOLUTION ≠ WRONG

The problem isn’t error. It’s resolution

One pixel

“Yellow.” True.

2 × 2

Yellow, with something dark on top. True.

4 × 4

It has ears. True.

12 × 12

You can start to tell.

The full sprite

Pikachu.

No step here is lying. Each one just sees less. Same with “worker”, “Gryffindor” or “Leo”: not wrong, just coarse.

Chapter 3/8 · 21%

Ask the audience at every step: is this a lie? No. The yellow square is completely right, Pikachu really is yellow. It just tells you almost nothing.

MEANWHILE, IN THE LIVING ROOM

And society keeps sorting

The same urge, outside academia.

Which house are you?

4 HOUSES

Courage, wisdom, loyalty or ambition

Which Friends character?

6 FRIENDS

Six familiar types from your living room

Which sign are you?

12 SIGNS

12 signs and four elements

The value

Identity and fun. People put “Slytherin” in their bio, and it really does say something about them.

The price

No nuance, and no connection between the types.

There’s also the Barnum effect: a vague enough description sounds accurate to everyone. PSP tries to be specific enough that you can disagree with it.

Chapter 3/8 · 22%

Don't dismiss them: they have real value, just like the fathers of sociology. The problem is the same problem: resolution. And here is what makes PSP different: not a box you're in or out of, but coordinates. 18 types, 6 stats and 5 ways to evolve combine into a profile, not a label.

PSP·04

Pokémon as a sociologist

The most detailed sorting we have: the most categories, and math that holds them together. Not a replacement for sociology, but a tool in its hands

Chapter 4/8 · 27%

WHY POKÉMON

Four reasons Pokémon is a good tool for sorting people

The most detailed

Marx has 2 classes, Hogwarts 4 houses. Pokémon: 600 different lines

The most mathematical

Every ability is a number, and every meeting between two types is a calculation. You can compute in advance who wins a battle

The most harmonious

30 years of calibration: no type is stronger than all the others, and every type has a weakness and an advantage

The most dynamic

Not just who you are today: evolution also describes how you change

Chapter 4/8 · 28%
<section id="d-battle"></section>

IT'S SUPER EFFECTIVE!

Same act, a completely different effect

How much one person’s actions affect another depends on both of their personalities. Just like an attack in Pokémon: the outcome depends on the type of the attacker and the type of the target.

×2

Ground vs. Electric. A grounded person who asks “so what’s the actual plan?” instantly brings whoever jumps from idea to idea back down to earth.

×½

Fire vs. Water. Sweeping enthusiasm meets a balanced person, anchored in their group, and is simply absorbed without leaving a mark.

×0

Psychic vs. Dark. Sophisticated psychological analysis and mind games don’t touch the cynical realist at all; they see right through them.

Chapter 5/8 · 35%

THE LINE IS THE UNIT

The unit is a whole line, and you go through it again in every framework

A person is the whole line, all the time. Your stage changes from one framework to the next, but your way of evolving stays the same. For example, one person who is the Mudkip line:

In the first week of a salsa class

Stage one: learning the steps

In the Friday football group, two years in

Stage two: already a mainstay

As the eldest sibling in the family

Final stage: at full power

Chapter 5/8 · 36%

PSP·06

The 18 types

A type is the power a person brings to the world, and also the map of who affects them and whom they affect. Each type also has its own stat profile.

Chapter 6/8 · 38%

TYPE CHART

324 matchups at a glance

Each row is a type that affects, each column a type that is affected. The order, from the top and from the left: Normal, Fire, Water, Electric, Grass, Ice, Fighting, Poison, Ground, Flying, Psychic, Bug, Rock, Ghost, Dragon, Dark, Steel, Fairy.

Green: double effect

Red: only half

Black: no effect

Notice: no row is all green, and no column is all red. Nobody affects everyone, and nobody is immune to everyone.

* The relations are taken from the game itself, unchanged.

The second type changes the map

Same attack, two Water Pokémon, and the exact opposite result.

Same with us: one trait can protect another trait’s weakness, or make it worse.

One slide instead of two. First the number: almost half of all Pokémon are dual types. Then the same Electric attack on two Water Pokémon: Quagsire’s Ground zeroes it, Gyarados’s Flying doubles it. The audience saw Gyarados fall in the battle, so it connects. Then the parallel to people.

WHO'S THAT TYPE? · RULES

Game: which type?

01

For each type, 3 characters appear one after another. The characters come up by themselves, every few seconds.

02

On your phone, pick which type it is. One guess per type, no take-backs.

03

The earlier you guess, the more you earn:

After one character: Ultra Ball

3

After two characters: Great Ball

2

After three characters: Poké Ball

1

04

A type that's already revealed drops off the list. At the end: the game champion.

DISCLAIMER

Every match of a person or character to a type is my personal opinion, not a ruling.

This is a deliberately simplified picture: every person, and every good character, is much more than one type.

Characters from real life and from culture: The Lord of the Rings, Game of Thrones, Harry Potter, Disney, Star Wars and more.

You're allowed, even encouraged, to disagree.
